papers.title: Finite speed Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-Kac processes and their applications in generative modeling
papers.abstract: We study the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-Kac (OU-K) process, where instead of a Brownian motion, a finite-speed Kac process defines the driving process. The OU-K process can be analyzed through a rescaled, time-inhomogeneous Kac process, characterized by a switching rate from the Kac part, and a convergence rate from the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU) part. The law of this inhomogeneous Kac process describes the solution of a wave equation, the Euler-Poisson-Darboux (EPD) equation. For Kac switching rates being multiples of the OU convergence rate, we can explicitly derive this EPD solution via the sum of (the derivative of) two Legendre polynomials, restricted between two Dirac points representing the wave fronts. Using the framework of piecewise-deterministic Markov processes (PDMP), we describe the conditional velocity fields of the OU-K process via our polynomial-law-formula. This allows us to apply the OU-K process in a generative flow model. Since the OU-K velocity fields prove to be bounded by the finite Kac speed, the usual time truncations of diffusion models become unnecessary. We demonstrate advantages over diffusion and flow matching models in terms of generation sharpness on singular data sets, while achieving competitive results on CIFAR-10 image generation.

papers.title: The $\alpha$-Limit Problem: Convergence of a Linear Degenerate Interface Transmission Problem
papers.abstract: We study the singular limit of a family of linear degenerate interface transmission problems arising from a regularization procedure in the newly proposed Two-Parameter Diffuse Domain Method (DDM2p). For $\alpha>0$, the regularized problem admits a strictly convex variational formulation on $H^{1}(\Omega)$. In the limit $\alpha\to0$, the problem degenerates to a weakly coupled interface system with a nonstandard energy structure. To characterize the limit, we introduce a closed Hilbert subspace $\mathcal{H}\subset H^{1}(\Omega)$, defined through an auxiliary Helmholtz problem on an annular subdomain $\Omega_2\subset \Omega$, and identify the limiting energy functional $\mathcal{E}_{0}$ on $\mathcal{H}$. We prove that the regularized energies $\mathcal{E}_{\alpha}$ restricted to $\mathcal{H}$ $\Gamma$-converge to $\mathcal{E}_{0}$ in the strong $L^{2}(\Omega)$ topology, using the standard framework. Consequently, minimizers of $\mathcal{E}_{\alpha}$ converge to the unique minimizer of $\mathcal{E}_{0}$, which is shown to be equivalent to the solution of the limiting interface problem. We further prove a strong convergence $u_{\alpha}\to u_{0}$ in $H^{1}(\Omega)$ and establish a convergence rate of $O(\alpha)$. Numerical experiments in one spatial dimension exhibit first-order convergence, suggesting that the proved $O(\alpha)$ upper bound is sharp.

papers.title: Dispersive decay for the modified Benjamin-Ono equation with small data
papers.abstract: We study the modified Benjamin-Ono equation for small, localized initial data where no solitons arise, and prove a dispersive estimate. Unlike the standard Benjamin-Ono equation, the modified version is not known to be completely integrable, so we cannot rely on integrable systems tools. First, to manage the nonlocal Hilbert transform in the linear part of the equation, we project the equation to positive and negative frequencies. We then combine wave packet testing of Ifrim-Tataru, the Klainerman-Sobolev vector field method, and a bootstrap argument.

papers.title: The Triangular Abrikosov Constant and the Thomas--Fermi $\Gamma$-Limit of Rotating Bose--Einstein Condensates
papers.abstract: We resolve the Abrikosov coefficient conjecture for rapidly rotating two-dimensional Bose--Einstein condensates within the variational framework of $\Gamma$-convergence. For a harmonic trap, we establish the $\Gamma$-convergence of the rescaled Gross--Pitaevskii energy functionals in the fast-rotation regime, through weak $L^2$ convergence of the rescaled densities, and identify the effective interaction coefficient $\beta_*$ with $b_\triangle$, the Abrikosov ratio associated with the triangular vortex lattice. The limiting Thomas--Fermi functional determines the first correction to the minimum energy and the macroscopic density of almost minimizers. For the auxiliary rescaled model and its lowest-Landau-level restriction, we also compute a strictly positive limiting $L^2$ distance between minimizing densities and the Thomas--Fermi profile. The identification of the effective interaction coefficient $\beta_*$ with the triangular Abrikosov ratio $b_\triangle$ relies on the sharp Gaussian-minorant theorem established in a recent OpenAI preprint~\cite[Theorem~1.2]{Atomic}. A Fourier representation of the quartic energy and a weighted Poisson identity yield a lower bound for arbitrary magnetic-periodic lowest-Landau-level states. The sign conditions on the minorant and its Fourier transform give the bound, while the lattice contact conditions identify its coefficient with $b_\triangle$. Cutoff and magnetic projection transfer this estimate to local holomorphic states without boundary conditions or periodicity assumptions. Consequently, the free-cell coefficients converge to $b_\triangle$ with error $O(L^{-1/5})$ on squares of side length $L$.

papers.title: Scattering for cubic and Yukawa--Hartree Dirac equations wiith polynomially decaying spacetime metrics
papers.abstract: We study massive Dirac equations in three space dimensions with small, time-dependent perturbations of the principal coefficients and decaying zeroth-order matrix terms. The principal perturbation and its spatial derivatives decay polynomially at rate $\rho>7/2$, and its first time derivative has one additional inverse spatial power. We prove small-data global well-posedness and scattering for local cubic nonlinearities in $H^s$, $s>1+5/(2(\rho-1))$, and for Yukawa--Hartree nonlinearities in $H^s$, $s>1/2+5/(2(\rho-1))$. The argument retains the coupling between the metric-adapted positive and negative branches. Its main ingredients are a time-independent modified energy, a weighted estimate controlling the full massive low-frequency component, and frequency-dependent spatial cutoffs. The operator class contains the geometric Dirac Hamiltonian of a synchronous spacetime metric with its full spin connection. No second time derivative, temporal integrability, or asymptotic stationarity is assumed. Scattering is formulated relative to the exact nonautonomous linear evolution.

papers.title: The retarded interaction and non-scattering for 3D Maxwell--Dirac system
papers.abstract: We prove an a priori obstruction to linear scattering for the massive Maxwell--Dirac system in three space dimensions. A global solution with nonzero charge cannot scatter linearly in $L^2$ if its full and homogeneous potentials are $O(t^{-1})$, and the homogeneous potential is $o(t^{-1})$ in compact timelike cones. No nonlinear asymptotic expansion is assumed in this non-scattering theorem. We also identify the exact leading interaction when the nonlinear current approaches a free Dirac current in $L^1$. Its coefficient is a positive quadratic form in the velocity density and is bounded below by the square of the charge divided by $4\pi$. The proof uses free Dirac asymptotics and an estimate for retarded source errors after pairing with a smooth free current. The main arguments, including the oscillatory retarded interaction, are proved here. Global existence and the required nonlinear decay remain separate inputs; a small-data application to existing theory is stated explicitly as such.

papers.title: Counterexamples to the clamped-plate eigenvalue ratio conjecture
papers.abstract: Ashbaugh in 1999 conjectures that the ball maximizes the ratio of the second to the first eigenvalue for the vibrating clamped-plate problem. We disprove this conjecture by constructing smooth connected domains in every dimension $d\ge2$. The construction starts with an interior sphere on which the displacement is required to vanish. The first two eigenvalues have the same relative increase at first order, but the second increases more at second order. This gives a strict increase of their ratio, which survives approximation of the sphere by finitely many codimension-two supports and their replacement by smooth holes. We identify the limiting Sobolev spaces through trace estimates and logarithmic cutoffs, and use the geometric construction for the buckling problem to obtain connected perforated domains.

papers.title: Pseudo-profiles for vectorial Allen-Cahn systems
papers.abstract: The purpose of the present paper is to present a new type of solutions to the elliptic vectorial Allen-Cahn system of equations. Its main feature is that in the classical rescaling its asymptotics do not follow the rule of balance of energies, which is crucial in the analysis of the asymptotics for the scalar problem.

papers.title: Dynamics of a single 3D vortex ring
papers.abstract:
We study the axisymmetric Navier--Stokes flow without swirl originating from a circular vortex ring. For each fixed $s\in(0,1)$ and sufficiently large circulation Reynolds number $\Gamma/
u$, we prove that, on the time scale $t\lesssim T_{m adv}(\Gamma/
u)^{s}$, the vorticity $\omega_	heta$ is approximated by a traveling wave solution featuring a Gaussian-type core with scale $O(\sqrt{
u t})$, whose off-axis distance remains constant and which continuously translates along the axial direction. In particular, the leading-order axial translation velocity is given by the Kelvin-Saffman formula. The proof relies on the approximation and Arnold energy framework of Gallay and \v{S}ver'ak \cite{GS2024}. We modify the weight used in \cite{GS2024} and estimate the relative-vorticity error to obtain favorable boundary dissipation at the symmetry axis and close the energy estimate.

papers.title: Brunn-Minkowski inequality for Riesz capacity in one dimension
papers.abstract: The Brunn-Minkowski inequality for Riesz $p$-capacity is proved on the line for every $p<1$ and all compact sets, including disconnected sets. For $-1<p<1$, equality holds exactly for a singleton summand or else two intervals, provided at least one capacity is positive. The proof couples equilibrium measures in increasing order.

papers.title: Strong solutions to the Cahn--Hilliard--Darcy--Forchheimer system for incompressible two-phase flows with a soluble surfactant
papers.abstract: We study a diffuse-interface model for incompressible viscous two-phase flows with a soluble surfactant in a bounded porous medium in two or three dimensions. The resulting system consists of a Darcy--Forchheimer equation for the seepage velocity $\bm{u}$ coupled with two Cahn--Hilliard equations, one for the difference in volume fractions of the two fluids denoted by $\phi$, and the other for the local concentration of the surfactant $\psi$. In the general scenario of non-constant coefficients and mobilities, we establish the existence of a local (resp. global) strong solution in three (resp. two) dimensions to the corresponding initial-boundary value problem with the no-flux boundary conditions for the phase-field variables and chemical potentials and a no-penetration condition for the velocity. In the case of constant coefficients in the Darcy--Forchheimer equation and constant mobilities in the Cahn--Hilliard equations, with a suitably large Forchheimer exponent, we establish the existence of a global strong solution in three dimensions. Furthermore, using the {\L}ojasiewicz--Simon approach, we prove the global existence of a unique strong solution when the initial data are sufficiently close to a local energy minimizer of the free energy.

papers.title: Co-rotating and traveling asymmetric vortex sheets for the planar Euler equation
papers.abstract: The aim of this paper is to construct co-rotating and traveling vortex sheet pairs with asymmetric configurations for the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equation. The vorticity of these solutions is concentrated on two small closed curves of different sizes, which carry vortex sheets of different circulations and either rotate uniformly about their centroid or translate with constant speed. The proof relies on the Birkhoff--Rott formulation of the problem and on the implicit function theorem at the point vortex pairs.

papers.title: The Dirichlet Problem for Quaternionic $k$-Hessian Equations
papers.abstract: We study the Dirichlet problem for quaternionic $k$-Hessian equations on smooth bounded domains. For a smooth positive density $f(q,z)$ satisfying $f_z\ge0$, we prove existence and uniqueness of a smooth admissible solution whenever a smooth admissible subsolution with the prescribed boundary values exists. The proof extends the quaternionic Monge--Amp\`ere subsolution method to $2\le k<n$ through boundary second derivative estimates. We also construct subsolutions on strictly quaternionic $(k-1)$-convex domains and characterize smooth solvability for constant boundary values.

papers.title: Existence and uniqueness of non negative radial solutions to semilinear elliptic problems on the exterior of a unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^2$
papers.abstract: We study the problem \begin{equation}\notag \begin{cases} - \Delta u &= \lambda K(x) f(u) \hspace{.1cm} \mbox { in } B_1 ^c, \\ u(x)&=0 \hspace{1.5cm} \mbox { on } \partial B_1, \end{cases} \end{equation} where $\lambda$ is a positive parameter, $B_1^c:=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^2:|x|>1\}$ is the exterior of the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^2$, $K:B_1^c\rightarrow (0,\infty)$ is a $C^1$ radial function and $f:[0,\infty)\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ is a $C^1$ concave function which is sublinear at infinity such that $f(0)<0$. We establish the existence and uniqueness of non negative radial solutions for large values of parameter $\lambda$. Moreover, we prove certain qualitative properties of nonnegative radial solutions for a class of problems in dimension 2. In contrast to the case $n\geq3$, where positive solutions decay to zero at infinity, we prove that non negative solutions are positive, radially increasing with the limit existing at infinity.

papers.title: Existence and regularity for a non-autonomous Born-Infeld equation with a confining potential
papers.abstract: We study the non-autonomous Born-Infeld equation $\operatorname{div}(Du/\sqrt{1-|Du|^2})-V(x)u+|u|^{p-2}u=0$ in $\mathbb R^N$, where $N\ge3$ and $2<p<2^*=2N/(N-2)$. For a $C^1$ potential satisfying $\inf V>0$, $V(x)\to\infty$ as $|x|\to\infty$, and $|x\cdot\nabla V(x)|\le C_DV(x)$ with $0\le C_D<p-2$, we prove the existence of a positive classical solution and infinitely many distinct nontrivial classical solutions. The argument combines the nonsmooth monotonicity trick with compactness induced by the confining potential. A Pohozaev-type identity yields uniform bounds for parameter-dependent critical points. A local minimization characterization identifies these critical points with weak solutions and establishes strict spacelikeness. Local Schauder estimates then give $C^{2,\alpha}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ regularity. All the solutions belong to the natural energy space $H_V^1(\mathbb R^N)$ and satisfy $|Du|<1$.

papers.title: Local well-posedness for the Novikov-Veselov equation at subcritical regularity
papers.abstract: We establish local well-posedness of the Novikov--Veselov equation (NV), at every fixed value of the energy parameter, for initial data in $H^s(\mathbb{R}^2)$ in the entire subcritical Sobolev range $s>-1$. The argument is perturbative and does not invoke the integrable structure, instead adapting the strategy in our previous work on KdV (2026). An infinite normal-form expansion indexed by binary trees is combined with a gauge transform that bypasses the obstructions in the associate bilinear estimate, and the resulting gauged equation -- carrying nonlinear contributions of every order -- is closed by a contraction in a Fourier restriction space. The analytic engine is a family of frequency-restricted multilinear bounds, supported by a detailed description of the two-dimensional resonance geometry attached to (NV).

papers.title: Stochastic Nonlocal Conservation Laws with L\'evy Noise: Stability, BV Estimates, and Vanishing Viscosity
papers.abstract: We study one-dimensional stochastic nonlocal conservation laws with a convolution-type interaction field, driven by multiplicative Brownian noise and compensated Poisson random measures. The nonlocal operator modifies the classical entropy structure, while the jump noise produces nonlinear correction terms in the entropy inequality. We introduce a notion of stochastic entropy solution and establish an $L^1$-stability estimate using spatial doubling of variables and the It\^o--L\'evy formula. This yields uniqueness in the vanishing-viscosity class and, under additional bounds, a localized Cauchy estimate of order $\sqrt{\varepsilon+\varepsilon'}$. Existence is obtained by vanishing viscosity: we construct the viscous solutions through a Faedo--Galerkin scheme and derive viscosity-uniform $L^1$ and localized $BV$ estimates, which allow us to pass to the limit and obtain a spatially $BV$ stochastic entropy solution.

papers.title: Stochastic inverse source problem in inhomogeneous media: far-field statistics
papers.abstract: This paper is concerned with an inverse random source problem for the stochastic Helmholtz equation in a known three-dimensional inhomogeneous medium. The source is driven by spatial white noise. We seek to recover its mean and strength from the mean and cross-frequency covariance of the far-field pattern. For a smooth nontrapping wave speed, we use the spectral measure of the acoustic operator to relate the far-field data to the source statistics. Under a priori regularity bounds, this relation gives conditional stability for the source mean and the source strength. We derive explicit reconstruction formulas for both quantities and bound the errors due to frequency truncation and data perturbations. We also obtain mean-square error bounds for reconstructions from finitely many independent experiments. Numerical experiments illustrate the reconstruction accuracy and the effects of bandwidth and sample size.

papers.title: Sharp Finite-Time Blow-Up for Unforced Axisymmetric Euler Without Swirl via Multiscale Data
papers.abstract: For the unforced Euler equations, we construct a compactly supported initial vorticity within the class of axisymmetric flows without swirl, whose solution blows up in finite time. The initial vorticity belongs simultaneously to every H\"older space $C^\alpha$, $\alpha<1/3$. This is sharp given that global regularity is known when $\alpha=1/3$ in the case of axisymmetric flows without swirl. Previous constructions by Shkoller \cite{Shk26}, Chen \cite{Chen26I,Chen26II}, and Shao--Wei--Zhang--Zhang \cite{SWZZ26} establish blow-up for each prescribed exponent $\alpha$ in the same sharp range. Our construction achieves simultaneous membership in all these spaces. In addition, our construction is short. Our proof uses multiscale initial data, in the spirit of Kim--Jeong~\cite{KJ22}, C\'ordoba--Mart\'inez-Zoroa--Zheng~\cite{CMZZ25}, and Bang--Cheskidov~\cite{BC26}. The blow-up mechanism is a forward cascade through successively smaller scales. A main difficulty in approaching the critical exponent $1/3$ is caused by large self-deformation. Our main idea to overcome this difficulty is to obtain a lower bound for strain at the stationary non-smooth point by using angular redistribution. A related outstanding open problem is to establish an unforced Euler blow-up from smooth data in the case of axisymmetric flows with swirl. A recent multiscale construction by OpenAI for the unforced Euler equations is, however, non-axisymmetric. Although we work in the no-swirl class, the axisymmetric multiscale mechanism developed here may offer a possible route toward the still-open problem of axisymmetric smooth blow-up.

papers.title: The Benjamin-Feir stability diagram for Stokes waves with constant vorticity in finite depth
papers.abstract: We determine the Benjamin-Feir stability diagram for small-amplitude Stokes waves with constant vorticity in finite depth. For the full water wave system, we derive an explicit instability index and rigorously classify its sign throughout the depth-vorticity plane. With gravitational acceleration and carrier wavenumber normalized to one, we identify a unique minimum depth $h_{\text{crit}}\approx1.36271$, below which Benjamin-Feir instability is absent for every vorticity. Above this depth, two vorticity thresholds delimit the unstable regime, outside of which the spectrum near the origin remains purely imaginary for all small Floquet exponents. In particular, at each fixed finite depth, constant vorticity of sufficiently large magnitude suppresses Benjamin-Feir instability. Moreover, any constant vorticity $\gamma\ge 2/\sqrt{3}$ suppresses Benjamin-Feir instability at every finite depth. The proof combines Hamiltonian spectral perturbation theory, symbolic computations, and formal verification in Rocq. Away from the transition set, our results rigorously confirm the stability criterion predicted by the nonlinear Schr\"odinger approximation of Thomas, Kharif, and Manna.

papers.title: Optimal polynomial decay and nonlinear stabilization for an indirectly damped wave-MGT system
papers.abstract: We study a conservative wave equation coupled to a dissipative Moore--Gibson--Thompson equation by a zero-order interaction that is symmetric in augmented variables. A general modal proposition relates the exact resolvent and semigroup asymptotic constants through an asymptotically unitary diagonalization. Its application to this system yields the optimal fourth-order resolvent estimate and the exact linear decay constants. These estimates lead to nonlinear stabilization from small regular initial data. On smooth bounded domains, a weighted composition estimate that accommodates a singular third derivative of the source at zero gives the optimal state rate $t^{-3/4}$ and energy rate $t^{-3/2}$ for power and logarithmic sources. In dimension three, the result includes $f(u)=|u|^q u$ with $3/2<q<2$ and $f(u)=|u|^{\gamma-2}u\log|u|$ with $7/2<\gamma<4$, within the source ranges of the companion general-source theory. Dimension-dependent extensions hold through dimension seven in the same data space, and in arbitrary dimension with higher regularity and a higher order of vanishing at zero. A lower-regularity graph-norm theorem and a conditional transfer theorem for general sources are also proved. Each nonlinear small-data decay exponent is optimal among uniform estimates with the stated dependence on the initial-data norm.

papers.title: Simultaneous recovery of elastic and viscous coefficients in a Kelvin-Voigt equation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the simultaneous recovery of a spatially dependent elastic coefficient and a time- and space-dependent viscosity coefficient in a scalar Kelvin-Voigt equation. We prove that the displacement-to-traction map over any fixed time interval uniquely determines both coefficients, provided that the Riemannian metric induced by the viscosity is simple at each time. In the velocity formulation, the elastic term gives rise to a Volterra memory term involving second-order spatial derivatives, with a corresponding memory contribution to the boundary traction. We first determine all normal derivatives of both coefficients at the boundary using highly oscillatory boundary data. We then construct exact parabolic exponential solutions in the presence of memory and determine the viscosity by boundary rigidity. With the viscosity determined, an approximate identity argument reduces recovery of the elastic coefficient to injectivity of the scalar geodesic ray transform. Finally, numerical experiments illustrate a regularized finite-dimensional reconstruction of both coefficients from finitely many moments of the displacement-to-traction map.

papers.title: The Capillary Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski Flows
papers.abstract: We study a capillary Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski flow on a non-obtuse spherical cap for $1\le k\le n-1$: \[ \partial_t h= \frac{h^2\varphi(\ell/h)}{f}\, \bar{\sigma}_k(\nabla^2h+h\sigma)-h, \qquad \nabla_\mu h=\cot\theta\,h. \] In the supercritical regime \[ a_\varphi(s)=\frac{s\varphi'(s)}{\varphi(s)} \ge k+1+\delta, \qquad s a_\varphi'(s)\ge0, \] we obtain time-uniform $C^0$ and $C^1$ estimates and a closed scalar equation for the speed ratio. A dynamic Orlicz square-completion identity, combined with inverse-concavity, yields a viscosity estimate for the minimum principal radius. Under a strict dynamic Orlicz-convexity condition and \[ \frac{f_\mu}{f}\ge\frac{n-k}{n}\cot\theta, \] we prove time-uniform two-sided principal-radius bounds on every smooth existence interval for $0<\theta\le\pi/2$ and deduce long-time existence and smooth convergence to a stationary solution. The boundary regularity step uses a quantitative interior concave estimate through Neumann reflection and a concave uniformly elliptic extension. Under the weaker condition $(f\ell^{k-1})_\mu\ge0$, strict convexity is preserved on every smooth existence interval. For $k=1$, the transformed scalar equation is uniformly parabolic for every $0<\theta<\pi$. Classical parabolic estimates then give an all-angle scalar flow theorem, without asserting geometric convexity preservation in the obtuse range.

papers.title: Inverse energy transfer for 2D Navier--Stokes near a self-similar vortex collapse
papers.abstract: We prove inverse energy transfer for the two-dimensional Navier--Stokes equations near a self-similar three-vortex collapse, confirming the 1979 prediction of Novikov and Sedov. Nonlinear interactions transfer kinetic energy from high to low frequencies over a common time interval that shrinks to the collapse time as the viscosity tends to zero. We prove that the net nonlinear transfer over this interval converges to the same positive constant across an expanding range of frequency cutoffs, with quantitative error bounds uniform in the cutoff.

papers.title: Nondegeneracy of the bubble for a fourth-order Liouville boundary problem
papers.abstract: We establish the nondegeneracy of the bubble for \[ \Delta^2u=0\quad \text{in }\mathbb R^4_+,\qquad \partial_tu=0,\quad \partial_t\Delta u=e^{24\pi^2u} \quad \text{on }\partial\mathbb R^4_+. \] Using Fourier analysis, stereographic projection and a removable-singularity argument, we classify the weighted $L^2$ boundary kernel without assuming boundedness of the boundary solution. This determines the bounded half-space kernel. Both kernels are generated by dilation and tangential translations. We further obtain sharp estimates for the projected spherical inverse.

papers.title: The Capillary Dual Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski Problem
papers.abstract:
We study a capillary dual Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski problem on a spherical cap. For $2\le k\le n$, $1<p<k+1$, and $0<	heta<\pi/2$, we consider \[ \sigma_k(
abla^2h+h\sigma) = f(\xi)h^{p-1} rac{ho^{k+1}}{\varphi(ho)}, \qquad ho=(h^2+|
abla h|^2)^{1/2}, \] with the capillary Robin condition $
abla_\mu h=\cot	heta\,h$. Assuming that $f$ is positive, smooth and horizontally even, $g=f^{-1/(p+k-1)}$ satisfies the capillary spherical-convexity and boundary compatibility conditions, and $H(r)=\varphi(r)/r^p$ is strictly increasing and proper with $Q_\varphi(r)\le k+1$, we prove the existence of a smooth, positive, horizontally even solution that is strictly capillary convex. The proof uses an Orlicz homotopy, uniform a priori estimates, a viscosity constant-rank argument when $k<n$, global oblique regularity, and degree theory.

papers.title: On the dynamics of N classical particles interacting with a complex environment
papers.abstract: The interactions of a particle with its environment eventually lead to the damping of its motion. This phenomenom is well understood when considering a single particle exchanging energy with the environment. The situation is definitely more complex when many particles are considered: the energy dissipation mechanisms are not clear whenever particles create a common well in which they keep interacting. In this framework, we identify the equilibrium solutions, that consist in clusters of particles at rest, and we establish their spectral stability. We show that the mean position/velocity pair is damped exponentially fast at the linearized level. Coming back to the non linear problem, we can show, at least in some simplified cases, that the dissipation mechanisms also involve far slower rates, that explain the difficulty in observing the relaxation behavior on the individual trajectories.

papers.title: The Capillary Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski Problem
papers.abstract: We study the Capillary Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski Problem on an acute spherical cap. For $1\le k\le n-1$, the equation is \[ h\,\varphi(\ell/h)\,\bar\sigma_k(\nabla^2h+h\sigma)=f, \qquad \nabla_\mu h=\cot\theta\,h, \] where $\ell$ is the support function of the unit capillary spherical cap. For $1\le k\le n-1$, this includes the capillary Christoffel--Minkowski and capillary $L_p$ Christoffel--Minkowski problems; the same density formally recovers the capillary Orlicz--Minkowski endpoint when $k=n$. We organize the theory in five parts. After recalling the elementary symmetric functions and the capillary support-function formalism, we review the capillary Orlicz--Brunn--Minkowski framework and introduce the intermediate-order Orlicz $k$-mixed functional and its Euler--Lagrange equation. In the supercritical regime \[ a_\varphi(t):=\frac{t\varphi'(t)}{\varphi(t)}\ge k+1+\delta, \] we derive uniform $C^0$, $C^1$ and $C^2$ estimates for positive $k$-admissible solutions. The same supercritical index produces a strictly coercive second variation and a spectral gap for the linearized Neumann operator. These facts lead to existence and uniqueness by a continuity method, quantitative stability of the solution map in both the datum and the Orlicz weight, and an open perturbative class of strictly convex non-power solutions. Under an additional capillary Orlicz-convexity condition on the datum, a full-rank argument upgrades the global admissible solution to a strictly convex capillary support function.

papers.title: Quantitative high-contrast homogenisation of composite media with highly anisotropic fibres
papers.abstract: This work concerns a non-uniformly elliptic second-order differential operator with periodic coefficients that describes a composite medium formed by a periodic array of highly anisotropic cylindrical fibres set in an isotropic matrix. The ratio of transverse to axial conductivity in the fibres is linked to the period of the coefficients through a `critical' high-contrast scaling, and the axial conductivity is allowed to vary along the fibres. As the period $\varepsilon$ tends to zero, ellipticity degenerates in the directions transverse to the fibres. We are concerned with the resolvent of this operator in the small-$\varepsilon$ limit. For fibres with constant axial conductivity, the two-scale limit of such problems was identified by Cherednichenko, Smyshlyaev and Zhikov (Proceedings of the Royal Society of Edinburgh: Section A Mathematics 136(1), 87--114 (2006)), and a full two-scale asymptotic expansion, with remainder estimates for smooth right-hand sides, was constructed by Cherednichenko (Asymptotic Analysis 49(1--2), 39--59 (2006)). In the non-constant axial conductivity setting, considered here, we approximate the resolvent in terms of the two-scale limit operator and prove that the error is order $\varepsilon$ in the operator norm, uniformly over right-hand sides in the unit ball of $L^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$; we also obtain order-$\varepsilon$ estimates for the reciprocals of the spectral band functions. This work builds on results announced, without proof, for fibres with circular cross-section in Cooper and Kamotski (Direct and Inverse Problems with Applications: Extended Abstracts of the 2024 GAP Center Summer School, pp.~69--75, Birkh\"auser (2026)).

papers.title: Normalized ground state solutions to the nonlinear Born--Infeld problem
papers.abstract: We study normalized solutions to the Born--Infeld problem \begin{equation*} -{\rm div}\left(\frac{\nabla u}{\sqrt{1-|\nabla u|^2}}\right)+\mu u=f(u)\ \hbox{ in }\mathbb{R}^N,\qquad \int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|u|^2\,dx=2m^2, \end{equation*} $N\ge3$, where $m>0$ is prescribed and $\mu>0$ is an unknown Lagrange multiplier. The nonlinearity $f$ is assumed to be superlinear at infinity, with no upper restriction on its growth, and to behave like $|s|^{p-2}s$ near zero, with $2<p<2^*$. Following a Lagrangian approach, we relate the action ground state level $a(\mu)$ of the prescribed frequency problem to the masses of its ground states by means of one-sided derivative formulas, which lead to the existence of normalized solutions. A distinctive feature of the Born--Infeld operator is that the gradient constraint makes the energy bounded from below on every mass sphere, even in the $L^2$-supercritical case. For $2+4/N\le p<2^*$ we obtain a threshold $c_*>0$ such that normalized action ground states exist for $m^2>c_*$, and none exist for $m^2<c_*$. In the $L^2$-subcritical case they exist for every $m^2>0$. We prove that every action ground state has constant sign and is radial up to a translation.
